walkthroughs.body_html:
Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Religion, Peace & Conflict — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Religion, Peace & Conflict brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Religion, Philosophy & Ethics: Religion, Peace & Conflict.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.

Five distinct arguments for God's existence: from motion, causation, contingency, gradation of being, and final causes/teleology — collectively forming Aquinas's natural theology, not a single argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five steps of one cosmological argument.
Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.

mcqs.q: What is the central principle of situation ethics?
options: Aquinas's Five Ways are five Christian sacraments.
The only intrinsically good thing is agape love; rules can be broken if doing so produces the most loving outcome in the situation.
Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
You should do whatever feels right in the moment.
